subject: SLO boundary & measurement carveouts for Hosted API
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@helionics.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Tom Rogers <tom.rogers@helionics.io>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — carveouts/measurement questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the roadmap walkthrough yesterday — the platform looks promising. As we prepare the internal procurement packet, a few follow-ups from our SRE and procurement teams on latency commitments:

- We saw the p50/p95 targets in the draft term sheet (p50=60ms, p95=250ms). Can you confirm whether these are global (cross-region) or per-region measurements?
- During scheduled maintenance and regional failovers, how does Redwood treat latency measurement windows? Are there carveouts for transient failovers or maintenance-induced routing shifts?
- We operate a mixed-burst pattern (regular baseline + planned midday spikes). Is there a way to exclude short bursts from p95 measurement if they're due to customer-initiated load tests or pre-agreed migrations?

Our legal wants clarity because the invoice credits tie to p95 breaches measured over rolling windows. If those windows are overly sensitive to ephemeral events, it could trigger spurious credits.

Can you propose a precise measurement policy and any exception paths for the first 90 days of onboarding?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Li
Head of Platform Engineering — Helionics
[sent from mobile]
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@helionics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — carveouts/measurement questions

Hi Sara — really appreciate the detailed questions. Below is a concise proposal we can include in the SLO addendum; happy to iterate.

1) Measurement scope:
- P50/P95 are reported per-region by default. We can provide a global aggregated view, but contractual credits are evaluated per-region to avoid cross-region masking.

2) Measurement windowing: 
- We use rolling 1-hour windows sampled at 1-minute granularity for p95. That means each minute contributes to the rolling distribution used to compute the percentile over the last hour.
- For p50 we publish an hourly median as an operational metric (not credit-triggering).

3) Planned maintenance & transient failover carveouts: 
- Planned maintenance windows (announced >=72h in advance) are excluded from credit calculation for the scheduled window.
- For transient failovers and regional routing flaps, we offer an automatic carveout if the customer opens a telemetry ticket within 4 hours and we confirm the incident was a routing event. This is intended to prevent short network-layer flaps from creating credit events.

4) Short burst exclusion (burst test policy):
- We propose a "burst carveout" for customer-initiated load tests: if the burst is announced 24h in advance and results in a sustained p95 degradation for <30 minutes followed by return to baseline, we will exclude up to two such events per quarter from credit calculation.

5) Onboarding grace period:
- First 30 days: a 14-day operational grace where minor p95 blips will not auto-trigger credits; beyond those 14 days, standard measurement applies.

6) Fallbacks and model-level variants:
- When we detect capacity pressure we may route to a compatible lower-latency model variant (different quantization/sequence length) rather than queue. We will document which model variants are credit-eligible; fallbacks are disclosed in the addendum.

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) and I can draft an SLO addendum PDF reflecting this language and share it as an attachment for your legal/procurement to review. Does this approach match what your procurement team needs for deterministic credit triggers?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Helionics SLO addendum — carveouts and credits

Folks,

Quick notes after Sofia's draft to Sara: a few product/legal items to weigh in on before we send the formal addendum to Helionics procurement.

- Rolling 1-hour window at 1-min granularity: Good default. Product: can we confirm the telemetry retention and exact sampling algorithm? Ops has an edge-case where sampling gaps during brief infra restarts bias p95 upward.
- Bursts: the proposed 30-minute exclusion + 2 events/qtr is generous. Finance will want an explicit definition of "sustained" (I suggest: >10 consecutive minutes above baseline p95).
- Grace period: legal prefers 30-day operational grace with 14-day soft window (no automatic credits) — i.e., 30-day onboarding, but auto-credits only kick in after day 14. That maps to our support load during ingest.
- Model fallbacks: ensure we enumerate credit-eligible routes. If we auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant for capacity reasons, credits shouldn't apply if latency stays within fallback SLAs. Karthik, can you list the variants and their targeted p95?

Can Marissa take the lead on incorporating finance/legal edits and produce a PDF we can attach? I can loop in Legal for wording on "telemetry ticket" and acceptable evidence.

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Sales Operations
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@helionics.io>, Tom Rogers <tom.rogers@helionics.io>, procure@helionics.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API SLO addendum (draft) — Helionics (attached)

Hi Sara / Tom,

Attached is a draft SLO addendum that reflects the measurement policy we discussed and the internal carveouts for planned maintenance, transient failovers, and announced burst tests. Key points in the draft: 

- p50 (operational median) published hourly; p95 (credit-eligible) computed on rolling 1-hour windows with 1-minute sampling.
- Credit triggers evaluated per-region; planned maintenance announced >=72h excluded.
- Transient routing flaps may be carved out if a telemetry ticket is opened within 4 hours; that ticket should include traces/headers demonstrating the routing symptom.
- Customer-initiated burst exclusion: up to two announced exclusions per quarter (announce >=24h) for events that cause >10 minutes of sustained p95 degradation.
- Onboarding: 30-day onboarding window; automatic credits only apply after day 14.
- Operational credits: formula documented in section 3.2 of the addendum.

Attachment: redwood-slo-addendum-v1.pdf (draft)

Please review and flag any legal/contractual items you want tightened. If this looks acceptable, we can push the final addendum into DocuSign and loop in your contracts team.

Thanks for the partnership — we want to make the measurement deterministic while avoiding surprise credits from ephemeral network events.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-slo-addendum-v1.pdf (PDF) — 2 pages, draft addendum with measurement examples and credit formula]
